name: Adult men · low-angle isometric shoulder abduction (n=12)
source: Gielo-Perczak K, Matz S, An KN (2006). Arm abduction strength and its relationship to shoulder geometry. Journal of Electromyography and Kinesiology 16(1):66–78. DOI 10.1016/j.jelekin.2005.05.004. Table 7, reported shoulder joint moment magnitudes (N·m), pooled by the two glenoid geometry group sizes (7 and 5). Twelve healthy men (mean age 40.5 years) performed right-arm maximal isometric abduction while standing in a frame that limited trunk lean. With the elbow straight and wrist neutral, they exerted lateral force on an instrumented handle at 5°–30° of arm elevation from the side in the frontal plane. The protocol derives joint moments from three-dimensional handle loads during a constrained lateral exertion.
